mnemonic: Written out by hand 手 on paper 紙 and put in an envelope, which almost nobody does any more. One turned up from a friend: てがみ.
sentence: 友人から手紙をもらいました。
sentence_meaning: I received a letter from a friend.

mnemonic: Her hand closes round your wrist and stays closed. Not a touch, a hold you would have to work at to get out of: つかむ.
notes: Near 使う つかう, to use, and 包む つつむ, to wrap, in sound and nothing else. 握る にぎる is the other grip, your own hand closing round something.
sentence: 彼女が僕の手を掴みました。
sentence_meaning: She gripped my hand.

mnemonic: Not family and not a friend, some other 他 person 人 in the world, and you would rather they did not have your address: たにん.
notes: Same 他 as ほか, another. As a word it means specifically not one of yours.
sentence: 私は他人に住所を教えたくない。
sentence_meaning: I don't want to tell other people my address.

mnemonic: How a thing measures up 格 and whether people like 好 what they see. He came through the door and the room decided he looked good: かっこう.
notes: Sits near 学校 がっこう and 結構 けっこう in sound. かっこいい, good looking, is this word. 形 かたち is the shape of a thing and 姿 すがた the figure of a person.
sentence: 格好のいい青年に会ったよ。
sentence_meaning: I met a good-looking young man.

mnemonic: Light 光 landing on something in a way that stops you where you stand. You were not looking for it, it simply came into view: こうけい.
sentence: 驚くような光景が目に入った。
sentence_meaning: I happened to see an astonishing sight.

mnemonic: He went for milk and bread and came home with neither, having not so much forgotten as never once thought of it: すっかり.
notes: Sounds like しっかり, firmly, and means nothing whatever like it.
sentence: 買い物をすっかり忘れていた。
sentence_meaning: I completely forgot the shopping.

mnemonic: Meat or fish, and the waiter is waiting. Two things on the table and you have to put a finger on one of them: どちら.
notes: The polite one. どっち is the casual version, and こちら, そちら and あちら are the rest of the set. どれ asks the same thing of a set you can see.
sentence: 肉と魚とどちらが好きですか。
sentence_meaning: Which do you prefer, meat or fish?

mnemonic: Somebody stood 立 up on a tree 木 to see 見 further down the road than you can from where you are. That is the entire job: おや.
sentence: 親の愛はありがたい。
sentence_meaning: We're grateful for our parents' love.

mnemonic: One stretch of time 時 handed straight on to the next 代, and this one belongs to the robots. Yours was the one before: じだい.
sentence: 今はロボットが働く時代です。
sentence_meaning: Now is the age of working robots.

mnemonic: You make 作 the plan before the fight 戦 rather than during it, and every one of them knows their part by Saturday: さくせん.
notes: Shares 戦 with 戦う たたかう and 戦闘 せんとう, which are the fighting. 作戦 is the thinking done beforehand.
sentence: 彼らは次の試合のために作戦を立てたのよ。
sentence_meaning: They came up with a strategy for the next game.

mnemonic: Nobody has told him anything and he is already clearing the desk in his head, because there is an outside chance the transfer comes through: もしかしたら.
notes: Sits with 多分 たぶん. 多分 is a fair bet, もしかしたら is a smaller chance being raised just in case.
sentence: もしかしたら来年転勤になるかもしれない。
sentence_meaning: It's possible that I might be transferred next year.

mnemonic: Old 古 grass 艹 chewed down to the stalk, and your stomach after a third helping. Not sharp pain, just everything gone wrong in there: くるしい.
notes: 難しい むずかしい is difficult to work out. 苦しい is difficult to bear. Near 詳しい くわしい in sound only.
sentence: 食べすぎておなかが苦しい。
sentence_meaning: I have eaten too much and my stomach hurts.

mnemonic: Sun 日 and moon 月 in the one character and both of them switched on at once. Hit the switch and the room turns into this: あかるい.
sentence: 電気を点けると、明るくなります。
sentence_meaning: If you turn the lights on, it gets bright.

mnemonic: Something big 大 shut inside a boundary 囗, and everything that followed came out of it. Somebody has to work out what it was: げんいん.
notes: 理由 りゆう is the reason you give for a thing. 原因 is what actually caused it. Near 全員 ぜんいん in sound.
sentence: この事故の原因は何ですか。
sentence_meaning: What's the cause of this accident?

mnemonic: The long strip under 下 the roof that is not a room, and everybody's shoes are along one side of it. Bathroom on the right: ろうか.
sentence: この廊下の右にトイレがあります。
sentence_meaning: There is a bathroom on the right of this hallway.

mnemonic: He nods at somebody across the bar without using a name, and the way he says it tells you what he thinks of him: そいつ.
notes: あいつ is over there, そいつ is nearer to you. 奴 やつ is the same idea with a character to write it.
sentence: そいつは誰だい。
sentence_meaning: Who's that guy?

mnemonic: Not this morning and not last week, a stretch of this same day already gone by 先. The permission came through then and he is telling you now: さきほど.
notes: Formal. さっき is the everyday version of the same stretch of time.
sentence: その件でしたら、先ほど上司から許可を得ております。
sentence_meaning: Regarding that matter, I obtained permission from my superior a little while ago.

mnemonic: A big 大 person 人, which is the whole of what the character claims, and the one telling you to listen. Nothing in it says wise: おとな.
notes: The reading is irregular and has to be learned whole, since neither 大 nor 人 is saying any part of おとな.
sentence: 大人の言うことを聞きなさい。
sentence_meaning: Listen to what adults say.

mnemonic: One person 人 and then the mark that says do that again 々, and now it is a whole village of them and every one is kind: ひとびと.
notes: 人間 にんげん is people as a species. 人々 is people as a crowd made of individuals.
sentence: あの村の人々はとても親切です。
sentence_meaning: People in that village are very kind.

mnemonic: A hand 扌 with nothing 無 in it and nothing behind it, going over the cat's head slowly. Barely contact at all: なでる.
sentence: 猫の頭を撫でてあげた。
sentence_meaning: I patted the cat's head.

mnemonic: You stand 立 the umbrella against the wall by the door and it stays exactly where you left it. Somebody had to do the standing: たてる.
notes: 立つ たつ is a thing standing on its own. 立てる is you standing it up.
sentence: ドアのところに傘を立てておきます。
sentence_meaning: I'll put my umbrella by the door.

mnemonic: He cooks about once a month and everybody acts surprised each time. Not never and not often, somewhere in the middle: たまに.
sentence: 彼はたまに料理をします。
sentence_meaning: He cooks occasionally.

mnemonic: A flat hand on somebody's back on a crowded platform, and the sign on the wall says not to. Weight going one way and not letting up: おす.
notes: 引く ひく is the pull on the other door.
sentence: 後ろから押すと危ないですよ。
sentence_meaning: Pushing from behind is dangerous.

mnemonic: Whatever went on in there, her spirit 気 came back out level 平 and her face is giving away none of it: へいき.
notes: Less calm as a mood than unbothered. 平気です is I am fine, it does not matter.
sentence: 彼女は平気な顔をしていた。
sentence_meaning: She looked as if nothing had happened.

mnemonic: A heart 心 with everything set against it 非, sat in the dark through the last twenty minutes of the film: かなしい.
notes: 寂しい さびしい is the lonely sort of sad, a room with nobody in it. 悲しい is grief, and it has a cause.
sentence: その映画はとても悲しかった。
sentence_meaning: That movie was very sad.

mnemonic: The sun goes round the back of a cloud 隠 and the whole field turns grey. Nobody moved it, it simply went out of sight: かくれる.
notes: 隠す かくす is you hiding something. 隠れる is the thing hiding itself, or just going out of view.
sentence: 太陽が雲に隠れた。
sentence_meaning: The sun hid behind the clouds.

mnemonic: Told his Japanese is good, he waves it off twice over. Less modesty than being able to see exactly how far off it still is: まだまだ.
sentence: A「日本語が上手ですね。」B「いいえ、まだまだです。」
sentence_meaning: A: Your Japanese is good.B: No, I still have a long way to go.

mnemonic: The word you open with when the whole room has turned round to look at you and you have forty minutes on robots to fill: みなさん.
notes: みんな is the casual everyone. 皆さん puts さん on it and is what you say to a room.
sentence: 皆さん、今日はロボットについて話します。
sentence_meaning: Everyone, today we will discuss about robots.

mnemonic: You put the thing back through the door 戸 it came out of. The conversation wandered off and somebody drags it back: もどす.
notes: 戻る もどる is you going back yourself. 戻す is putting something else back. 帰る かえる is going home and 返す かえす is giving a thing back to its owner.
sentence: 話を戻しましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's return to the subject.

mnemonic: The war 戦 as a whole is one thing. This is the part where people are actually going at each other 闘, and the town is full of the wounded: せんとう.
notes: 戦い たたかい is the battle in the broad sense. 戦闘 is the combat itself, and 作戦 さくせん is the plan behind it.
sentence: 戦闘で多くの市民が傷付きました。
sentence_meaning: A lot of civilians were wounded in combat.

mnemonic: Sparks going off both sides of it and the pan beginning to catch. Get it turned off before the alarm starts: ひ.
notes: Same reading as 日 ひ, day or sun. 日 is the one up in the sky and 火 is the one on the stove.
sentence: 火を消して。
sentence_meaning: Put the fire out.

mnemonic: Two lots of fire 火 stacked up in the one character, and one candle throws enough of it to light the whole room: ほのお.
notes: 火 ひ is the fire itself. 炎 is what comes off it.
sentence: ろうそくの炎が部屋を照らしたんだ。
sentence_meaning: The candle's flame lit the room.

mnemonic: The heart 忄 goes first and the body follows, locked solid where it stands. Not nerves, the kind that stops you moving at all: きょうふ.
notes: 怖い こわい is the everyday scared. 恐怖 is the noun, terror, and 恐ろしい おそろしい is the adjective for whatever is causing it.
sentence: 余りの恐怖に体が強張った。
sentence_meaning: My body went stiff with such terror.

meaning: to be perplexed, to get lost
mnemonic: Rice 米 spilled the length of the road 辶 and every grain the same as the next. Twenty minutes of walking and none of it familiar: まよう.
sentence: 道に迷いました。
sentence_meaning: I lost my way.

mnemonic: He hands the report across and waits, and the only thing he wants back is the one word that means it will do: よろしい.
notes: Formal, and usually spoken downward, by a teacher or a boss. いい is the everyday version. 結構 けっこう and 平気 へいき also gloss as all right and mean different things.
sentence: レポートはこれでよろしいですか。
sentence_meaning: Is this all right as a report?

mnemonic: The moment the parts line up 機 and the right people happen to be in the room together 会. There have been a great many of those lately: きかい.
notes: 場 ば on its own is the occasion rather than the chance to act on it.
sentence: この頃、お酒を飲む機会が増えました。
sentence_meaning: These days, I have more occasions to drink alcohol.

mnemonic: Whatever it was in the dream, it was still in the room when you woke and the light had to go on. Not startling, the other kind: おそろしい.
notes: Shares 恐 with 恐怖 きょうふ, fear. 恐怖 is what you feel and 恐ろしい is what the thing is.
sentence: 昨夜恐ろしい夢を見た。
sentence_meaning: I had a frightening dream last night.

mnemonic: A person 亻 who lent you something long ago 昔 and has not forgotten it. Money off a friend is still money off a friend: かりる.
notes: The taking side of the arrangement. The lending side is 貸す かす.
sentence: 友達にお金を借ります。
sentence_meaning: I will borrow money from a friend.

mnemonic: Whatever it was is outside 外 of where it was a second ago, and his glasses are in his hand instead of on his face: はずす.
notes: Near 話す はなす and 離す はなす in sound and in nothing else.
sentence: 彼はメガネを外しました。
sentence_meaning: He removed his glasses.

mnemonic: The earth 土 underneath everything, and the particular patch of it where a man spent the whole rest of his life: ち.
notes: Same reading as 血 ち, blood. 地 has 土 earth in it, which is the entire difference. ところ and 場所 ばしょ are the everyday words for a place, and 場 ば leans towards the occasion.
sentence: 彼はその地で残りの生涯を過ごしたんだ。
sentence_meaning: He spent the rest of his life in that place.

mnemonic: A bundle 束 going down the road 辶 strapped tight so that nothing on it slows it down. He is at the far end before anybody: はやい.
notes: Same reading as 早い はやい, early. 早い is about the clock and 速い is about the speed. Arriving early is 早い, running fast is 速い.
sentence: 彼は走るのが速い。
sentence_meaning: He runs fast.

mnemonic: An arrow 矢 stood up next to a bean 豆 to settle which of them is which. She had the lot cut off in the summer: みじかい.
notes: 低い ひくい is short in height. 短い is short in length, or in time.
sentence: ララちゃんは髪が短いです。
sentence_meaning: Lara-chan's hair is short.

meaning: to like, to be pleased with
mnemonic: The thing gets in 入 past your guard and settles into your spirit 気, and now the new shoes are being worn indoors: きにいる.
notes: Literally it enters your 気. Settled and more particular than 好き: it is about one thing rather than a taste in general.
sentence: 新しい靴がとても気に入りました。
sentence_meaning: I really like my new shoes.

mnemonic: You take the self 己 that turned up last time and give it a knock 攵, then put the question again from the top: あらためて.
notes: Not simply again. It is doing the thing over properly and from a clean start, and it is formal.
sentence: 改めてあなたのご意見を聞かせてください。
sentence_meaning: Please let me hear your opinion once more.

mnemonic: Traffic on that street from five in the morning, and by the third day it is not the volume, it is that it will not stop: うるさい.
notes: Also said straight at people. うるさい on its own is be quiet.
sentence: この通りは車の音がうるさい。
sentence_meaning: Traffic is noisy on this street.

mnemonic: You aim, and it lands square 当 on the spot, and the spot this time was your friend's head. It does guessing right as well: あてる.
notes: 当たる あたる is the ball hitting on its own. 当てる is you hitting something with it.
sentence: ボールを友達の頭に当ててしまった。
sentence_meaning: I hit my friend’s head with a ball.

mnemonic: Paper folded right over the thing until none of it is showing, and the ribbon goes on last of all: つつむ.
notes: Near 掴む つかむ, to grip, in sound and nothing else.
sentence: プレゼントをきれいな紙で包みました。
sentence_meaning: I wrapped the present in beautiful paper.

mnemonic: Where a person 亻 is standing 立 and where a thing has been put 置, which between them is all that position means. North of Tokyo, on the map: いち.
notes: Same reading as 一 いち, one. 立場 たちば is where you stand in an argument and ところ is a place loosely. 位置 is where a thing sits on a map.
sentence: 私の町は東京の北に位置します。
sentence_meaning: My town is located north of Tokyo.

mnemonic: Down you go on the step and your knee finds the edge of it. Contact with the whole of your weight behind it: うつ.
notes: 当てる あてる is hitting a target you aimed at, 叩く たたく is knocking or tapping, 打つ is a solid blow.
sentence: 転んでひざを打ちました。
sentence_meaning: I fell down and hit my knee.

mnemonic: The eye 目 picks the thing out and the finger 指 goes up at it, and everything after that is walking toward it. Chef, one day: めざす.
notes: 目的 もくてき is the aim itself, the thing you want. 目指す is heading for it.
sentence: 私は料理人を目指しています。
sentence_meaning: I intend on becoming a cook.
